phase_name: Authority Evaluation Integration Prerequisite Decision Architecture
summary: Phase 147J.0 was authorized, following Phase 147I's CORE OPERATIONALLY READY -- INTEGRATION ARCHITECTURE NOT READY verdict, to resolve the four architectural prerequisite decisions 147I identified as blocking a future integration-architecture phase: claimed_identity ownership, Decision Template resolution ownership, evidence_kind compatibility across the nine governing contracts, and the two-stage evaluation model. Two parallel read-only research agents re-grounded the analysis directly against AEMIC-001 v1.2 and CHGR-001 v1.2 contract text (not only 147I's v1.0/v1.1-era paraphrase) and the actual authority_evaluation/interactive_workflow/governance.publication/cltr code. Decision A (claimed_identity) resolved to Session.owner_identity, no new field, directly grounded in AEM-REQ-014 and AEMIC-REQ-019's own parameter table, which already name Session.owner_identity as the source and state the package collects nothing. Decision B (Decision Template resolution) resolved to a single dedicated resolution capability, co-owned with Registry resolution by one future orchestration component, preferring a schema-artifact (Option C) Registry that derives both the EligibleAuthorityDeclaration and citation_text from one resolved document so template_ref/template_version/citation_text remain singular by construction. Decision C (evidence_kind) resolved as no compatibility issue: AEM-001/AEMIC-001 define no evidence_kind concept at all (zero occurrences), while CHGR-001/IWC-001/PEC-001/IWPC-001 share one consistent closed two-value enum (typed_confirmation_only/os_authenticated_user) serving assurance-level derivation only, a field the two never intersect. Decision D (two-stage evaluation) confirmed necessary, grounded in IWPC-REQ-144/147's disclosure that everything upstream of Publication's own O_CREAT|O_EXCL commit point is not authority-relevant; Stage 2 was explicitly determined to always supersede Stage 1 for citation purposes. Produced a decision interaction matrix identifying Decision B as foundational, a Registry boundary statement (without designing the Registry itself), an authoritative seven-input ownership table with exactly one owner per input, a three-strategy integration comparison selecting a dedicated Authority Evaluation Service (Strategy A) over Workflow-owned (Strategy B, over-coupling risk) and Publication-owned (Strategy C, directly forbidden by PEC-REQ-115/116 without an amendment this phase cannot make), and a preferred direction requiring no src/pcae/** change, no Session/readiness-package/CHGR/IWC/IWPC/PEC schema or contract amendment for the citation-only integration path identified. Overall Verdict: INTEGRATION PREREQUISITES RESOLVED WITH OBSERVATIONS. Full detail in docs/PHASE_147J0_AUTHORITY_EVALUATION_INTEGRATION_PREREQUISITE_DECISION_ARCHITECTURE.md.

validation_results.name: phase_147j0_decision_a_claimed_identity
validation_results.result: Resolved: Session.owner_identity is the claimed_identity source, per AEM-REQ-014 and AEMIC-REQ-019's own parameter table (report section 3), with IWC-REQ-036/037 establishing it as immutably bound at session creation. No new Session field introduced; this phase ratifies an already-contract-named source rather than inventing one.

validation_results.name: phase_147j0_decision_b_template_resolution
validation_results.result: Resolved: a single dedicated Decision Template resolution capability, co-owned with Registry resolution, deriving both the EligibleAuthorityDeclaration and citation_text from one resolved document, preferring a schema-artifact Registry (Option C) over an independent filesystem Registry (Option B) specifically because Option C structurally guarantees template_ref/template_version/citation_text singularity (report section 4).

validation_results.name: phase_147j0_decision_c_evidence_kind
validation_results.result: Resolved: no compatibility issue exists. Direct grep confirmed AEM-001/AEMIC-001 define no evidence_kind concept (zero occurrences); CHGR-001/IWC-001/PEC-001/IWPC-001 share one closed two-value enum used only for assurance-level derivation, a concept the two never intersect. No amendment required (report section 5).

validation_results.name: phase_147j0_decision_d_two_stage_evaluation
validation_results.result: Resolved: two-stage evaluation confirmed necessary, grounded in IWPC-REQ-144/147's disclosure that everything upstream of Publication's own commit point is not authority-relevant. Stage 2 explicitly determined to always supersede Stage 1 for citation purposes, per CHGR-REQ-097's surface-not-silently-resolve mandate (report section 6).

recommended_next_phase: Recommended next phase: 147J (Authority Evaluation Integration Architecture), which shall define only the architecture for integrating the verified standalone Authority Evaluation Model into PCAE -- orchestration ownership (the dedicated Authority Evaluation Service selected in this phase), Registry interaction, lifecycle boundaries (the two-stage model resolved in this phase), persistence, replay semantics, schema impacts, and consumption rules -- remaining architecture-only throughout and not implementing integration or amending contracts. This recommendation is not an authorization.
